questions.q: What does a Reserved Instance / Azure Reservation actually commit you to, in exchange for its discount?
options: A specific instance type (or family) and region for a 1- or 3-year term, with no interruption risk once it's running
A dollar-per-hour of compute spend that applies automatically across any instance type
A guarantee that the provider will never reclaim the capacity, applied to unused data center capacity
Nothing — Reserved Instances carry no commitment term at all
questions.explain: A Reserved Instance/Reservation locks in a specific instance type and region for 1 or 3 years at a lower rate; the running capacity behaves exactly like on-demand with zero interruption risk.

questions.q: How does a Savings Plan differ from a Reserved Instance?
options: A Savings Plan has no commitment term, while a Reserved Instance always requires one
A Savings Plan commits to a dollar-per-hour of compute spend and applies the discount across eligible instance types, rather than locking in one specific type
A Savings Plan can only be used with Spot capacity, never with on-demand instances
A Savings Plan guarantees a deeper discount than any Reserved Instance in all cases
questions.explain: A Savings Plan commits to a spend level, not a specific instance type/family, so the discount survives resizing or replatforming — at a slightly smaller discount than a matching Reserved Instance.

questions.q: Which workload is a genuinely appropriate fit for Spot / Azure Spot VM capacity, according to this lesson?
options: A single-instance customer-facing web application with no redundancy
A stateful database primary with no replica
A queue-backed batch worker pool that can lose an individual instance without anyone noticing
Any workload, as long as the discount is large enough to justify the risk
questions.explain: Spot fits workloads that are genuinely fault-tolerant — a queue-backed worker pool simply drains slower if one instance is reclaimed, which is a handled event rather than an incident.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say to right-size a workload (Lesson 21) before buying a Reserved Instance or Savings Plan for it?
options: Cloud providers require a right-sizing certificate before allowing any commitment purchase
Right-sizing is unrelated to commitment purchases and the ordering doesn't matter
Reserved Instances and Savings Plans automatically right-size the instance for you after purchase
Committing to a discount on an oversized instance locks in the wasted capacity for the whole commitment term
questions.explain: A commitment discount reduces the rate you pay for a given size — it doesn't change the size. Committing before right-sizing just locks in whatever waste already existed.

questions.q: What is the real operational risk of Azure Spot VMs or AWS Spot Instances that this lesson emphasizes?
options: They cost more per hour than on-demand instances of the same size
The provider can reclaim the capacity with very short notice — commonly around two minutes — whenever it's needed elsewhere
They cannot be used for any kind of batch or background processing
They require a 3-year minimum commitment before the discount applies
questions.explain: Spot capacity is unused capacity sold at a steep discount with no uptime guarantee; the provider can evict it on short notice, which is why only genuinely fault-tolerant workloads belong on it.
